content.thinking:
I'll design the scythe standing upright on a plinth base so it touches the floor, roughly 2 meters tall overall with the blade curving out near the top of the vertical shaft.

Now I'm planning the parts: a stepped octagonal plinth with glowing runes, a dragonbone-style shaft with a slight S-curve built from a swept path and vertebra-like rings along its length, leather grip wraps with gold bands, and a dragon-skull finial at the top with horns near where the blade attaches.

For the blade itself I'm working out the crescent outline directly in the xy-plane—plotting the convex outer edge and the inner edge with coordinates that curve out from the shaft and sweep forward to a sharp tip, making sure the inner edge stays below the outer edge to avoid self-intersection.

Setting bevel to 0.004 and thinking through the blade's color treatment, I want a bone-white base that glows teal near the cutting edge. Rather than a complex gradient paint function, I'll add a separate thin extrusion along the inner edge as a glowing cyan strip to simulate the sharpened blade line.

Still writing geometry...

For the dragonbone variant, I'm adding serrated spikes along the outer edge of the blade using the path's tangent to compute outward normals, plus curved horns sweeping back from the skull collar at the top of the shaft.

I want the skull snout pointing forward with horns sweeping back and up, glowing eye sockets, teeth spikes, and a separate jaw, with the blade emerging from the collar below it. I'm also adding a tattered teal-purple ribbon swept with catmull curves hanging below the skull, plus glowing soul-wisp spheres floating around the blade.

I'm scattering five small teal-glowing wisps with spike-cone tails near the inner edge of the crescent blade, then building the plinth base with stepped layers from y=0 to 0.14, a socket for the shaft, and a gold spike cap sunk at the bottom. I'm also finalizing the color palette, keeping it under 64 colors with bone, gold, and teal tones plus their shaded variants.

Setting up imports...

Setting up the root joint and building the plinth with a lathed stone outline plus a glowing rune ring made from a rotated torus...

Still placing gold studs... Now building the spine shaft as a swept rod with varying radius for a bone-like taper, then starting on the vertebrae segments stacked along it.

Building vertebrae and spike positions, skipping the leather grip zone, with small lateral bone spikes projecting front and back at each segment.

Now I'm designing the grip: a leather-wrapped rod with gold rings at each end, applying wine-colored diagonal wrap stripes, then starting on the gold butt cap cone at the base.

Working out the gold sleeve, decorative ring, and base collar flare, then shaping the top gold collar using a lathe profile around the blade root before positioning the skull head center for the cranium sphere.

Now I'm shaping the snout and lower jaw using frustum shapes with tapering radii, then placing upper teeth as small downward spikes along the jawline at regular intervals.

Still writing creature geometry...

Adding gold clamp bands near the blade root, then thinking through a center ridge rod along the blade using a curved sweep path between outer and inner edges, colored with the bone tone.

Now I'm working out the outer edge spike geometry — defining the outer catmull curve points and adjusting for how the extrude smoothing pulls the surface slightly inward from that curve, so I'm embedding the spike bases a touch deeper to compensate. I'm placing six serrated bone-colored spikes along the blade's outer edge, angling each one outward with a backward tangent blend for a curved, aggressive look.

Still writing blade outline coordinates...

Adjusting the glowing edge sliver to protrude slightly beyond the blade boundary, shifting points down so it reads as an energy edge rather than overlapping and flickering with the blade's inner face.

Checking the sliver polygon doesn't self-intersect at the tip, confirming the glow mesh uses a flat teal color with zero smoothing, and now planning rune decal planes on both blade faces using small SVG glyphs with teal strokes.

Now I'm adding glowing wisps nestled in the crescent hollow beneath the blade—small teal spheres with downward-leaning spike tails, maybe considering thin tether rods connecting them back to the blade edge for cohesion.

Then I'm building hanging cloth ribbons from the collar using a curved path with varying ellipse-radius taper, colored purple, ending in gold tassel spheres and small charms—gold torus rings plus glowing teal gem spheres at the tips.

Adding teal gem spheres at the collar front and extra gold filigree band cylinders along the shaft at higher positions, skipping the wire spiral idea. I'm checking plinth decoration—deciding to use studs instead of octagon-face boxes for the glowing slots—and confirming overall height comes out to about 2.12 units from floor to the topmost skull/blade point.

Now I'm wiring up the wisp tether rods and double-checking unused variables and typing in the loop, then moving to the lathe plinth's material paint and verifying the bracket geometry and sweep function signatures for the shaft, using a bone mottle texture for the color, with flat caps on both ends. Writing the horn sweep along a bezier curve...
